# SOP-P2-L1-04 Shift handover - Hot Forge line

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P2, line P2-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L1-RR01, EQ-P2-L1-IH02, EQ-P2-L1-SB03  
Related: MM-P2-L1-SB03, QS-PROC-06, SOP-P2-L1-02

Purpose
1. Provide a consistent, auditable process for shift-to-shift handover on the Hot Forge line to maintain safety, quality, and uptime. This procedure applies to operators, lead hands, and maintenance personnel responsible for EQ-P2-L1-RR01, EQ-P2-L1-IH02, and EQ-P2-L1-SB03.

Preconditions
2. The outgoing operator must complete all running checks and document status in the shift log before initiating handover.  
3. All safety incidents, near-misses, and equipment status changes must be entered into the incident register referenced by QS-PROC-06 prior to the handover.  
4. Any outstanding maintenance work on equipment named in this document must be raised as an active work order and referenced to MM-P2-L1-SB03.

PPE
5. Minimum personal protective equipment for handover personnel: steel-toe footwear, safety glasses, hearing protection, heat-resistant gloves, and face shield as required when entering hot zones. See SOP-P2-L1-02 for specific PPE allocation per task.

Procedure — numbered steps
6. Step 1 — Prepare documentation and records
   6.1. Outgoing operator assembles the shift log, start/stop records, any deviation reports, and current production count.  
   6.2. Verify that the log includes entries for EQ-P2-L1-RR01, EQ-P2-L1-IH02, and EQ-P2-L1-SB03. If maintenance actions occurred, attach the related MM-P2-L1-SB03 work order number.

7. Step 2 — Perform critical equipment status checks (outgoing)
   7.1. Confirm that EQ-P2-L1-IH02 coil cooling water flow meets operational minimum: The coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P2-L1-IH02) is 55 L/min. Document measured flow in the log.  
   7.2. Inspect EQ-P2-L1-SB03 blast wheel liner condition and verify fastener security: The blast wheel liner bolt torque for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P2-L1-SB03) is 50 N·m. Record verification and who performed the check.  
   7.3. For EQ-P2-L1-RR01, confirm run roll status, any abnormal vibration, and that no un-cleared jams are present; record observations.

8. Step 3 — Communicate process and product status
   8.1. Outgoing operator provides a concise summary: product type being processed, any process parameter deviations, scrap counts, and quality holds. Include references to QS-PROC-06 where quality issues require non-conformance handling.  
   8.2. Highlight any transient conditions or recurring adjustments that the incoming operator should monitor. Use one-line examples: e.g., "intermittent under-temperature events resolved by reducing feed, see log entry."

9. Step 4 — Confirm recent maintenance and modifications
   9.1. Review completed and pending maintenance from MM-P2-L1-SB03. Confirm that all safety guards are reinstalled and lockout/tagout procedures are cleared.  
   9.2. If any weld repairs, liner replacements, or bearing changes were performed, confirm the responsible technician has signed the work order and that the post-maintenance inspection is attached.

10. Step 5 — Handover of controls and verification (incoming)
    10.1. The incoming operator physically inspects the control panel and verifies indicator states against the outgoing operator’s checklist.  
    10.2. Incoming operator independently confirms the coil cooling water flow for EQ-P2-L1-IH02 and the blast wheel liner bolt torque for EQ-P2-L1-SB03 if these were cited in the log, and signs the verification entry.

11. Step 6 — Risk items and escalation
    11.1. Identify and list any unresolved safety risks or process risks. For any issue affecting quality, notify Quality per QS-PROC-06.  
    11.2. If a mechanical hazard is identified that cannot be immediately mitigated, escalate to maintenance and reference MM-P2-L1-SB03 for raising a corrective work order.

Rationale and background
12. Consistent, face-to-face handovers reduce miscommunication and prevent latent failures from propagating between shifts. Recording measured values for critical systems (for example the coil cooling water flow minimum for EQ-P2-L1-IH02 is 55 L/min and the blast wheel liner bolt torque for EQ-P2-L1-SB03 is 50 N·m) ensures that incoming operators have actionable verification points rather than subjective descriptions. Refer to SOP-P2-L1-02 for role definitions and QS-PROC-06 for non-conformance handling.

Examples and acceptable entries
13. Example shift log entries:
    13.1. "EQ-P2-L1-IH02: Coil cooling water measured 60 L/min at 07:45; no trips. See entry #42."  
    13.2. "EQ-P2-L1-SB03: Liner bolts checked and torque recorded at 50 N·m; no abnormal noise observed."  
    13.3. "EQ-P2-L1-RR01: Minor slip observed, cleared; monitor feed rate."

Records to keep
14. Maintain the following records attached to the shift log:
    14.1. Signed handover checklist.  
    14.2. Measurement logs for critical items (coil cooling water, liner bolt torque confirmation).  
    14.3. Copies of any MM-P2-L1-SB03 work orders opened or closed during the shift.  
    14.4. Quality reports referencing QS-PROC-06 when applicable.

Sign-off
15. Both outgoing and incoming personnel must sign and date the handover checklist. The lead operator or supervisor must co-sign to acknowledge receipt of all critical items and confirm that any safety or quality escalations have been actioned or assigned. Store the signed checklist with the shift log in the document control system.

Audit and compliance
16. Routine audits will sample handover checklists to validate compliance with this SOP and cross-check entries against MM-P2-L1-SB03 and QS-PROC-06 records. Non-compliance will be handled per QS-PROC-06.

Revision history
17. Revision history and changes must be recorded in the document control system per SOP-P2-L1-02.
